# Temple Scroll Column 64 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 64 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**64:1** You shall not neglect the Levite who resides within your gates, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.

**64:2** At the end of every three years you shall bring out the full tithe of your produce for that year and store it within your gates.

**64:3** The Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance with you, together with the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow within your gates, shall come and eat their fill,

**64:4** so that I may bless you in all the work of your hands.

**64:5** At the end of every seven years you shall grant a remission of debts. This is the nature of the remission: every creditor shall remit the claim he holds against his neighbor. He shall not press his neighbor or his brother for payment,

**64:6** for the remission of the LORD has been proclaimed. From a foreigner you may exact payment, but whatever claim you hold against your brother, your hand shall release.

**64:7** If a man is found kidnapping any of his brothers from among the children of Israel, and he enslaves him or sells him, that kidnapper shall die. So you shall purge the evil from your midst.

**64:8** If a man has committed a crime deserving the sentence of death, and he is executed, and you hang him on a tree,

**64:9** his body shall not remain on the tree overnight. You shall bury him that same day, for one who is hanged is accursed of God.

**64:10** You shall not defile your land, which I am giving you as an inheritance.

**64:11** If a man acts as an informer against his people, betraying his people to a foreign nation, and works evil against his people,

**64:12** you shall hang him on a tree so that he dies. By the testimony of two witnesses or by the testimony of three witnesses

**64:13** he shall be put to death, and they shall hang him on the tree.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 64 contains the Temple Scroll's most distinctive legal innovation. While Deut 21:22–23 prescribes hanging as post-mortem display ("he is put to death, and you hang him"), 11QT 64:11–13 reverses the order: "you shall hang him on a tree so that he dies" — making hanging the method of execution itself. This is the earliest Jewish text to prescribe what amounts to crucifixion. The Nahum Pesher (4Q169) likely references this law in connection with Alexander Jannaeus. "Informer" for רכל; "betraying" makes the treason explicit. "Accursed of God" (קללת אלהים) — the ambiguity of the Hebrew genitive (cursed BY God or a curse AGAINST God) is preserved.*
